## BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT
Oracle Retail Insights

## Merchandising Analysis
Merchandising Sales & Profit Subject Area

## 1. Purpose & Scope
This Business Requirements Document (BRD) defines the functional requirements for the Merchandising Sales & Profit subject area within Oracle Retail Insights (RI). It covers the predefined dashboards and reports under the Merchandising Scorecard and Merchandising Analysis sections, the key metrics, dimensions, and non-functional requirements.

## 1.1 In-Scope
Merchandising Scorecard – Merchandise Sales and Profit dashboard (Current Top 10 Sale Items, Current Sales & Profit Contribution) Merchandising Scorecard – Markdowns dashboard (Current Markdown Scorecard – Markdown to Sales Ratio) Merchandising Scorecard – Merchandise Performance dashboard (Season Performance) Merchandising Analysis – Merchandising Location Analysis dashboard (Daily Sales & Profit, Current Sales Projection) Sales & Profit metrics, Cost/Profit metrics, Markdown/Markup metrics, and Sales Forecast metrics Retail Merchandise Insights subject areas: As-Is, As-Was, and Point in Time

## 1.2 Out of Scope
Customer Analysis, Market Basket Analysis, Consumer, Cluster, and Wholesale dashboards Inventory, Supplier, and Customer Order reporting areas

## 2.1 Module Overview
The Merchandise Insights module provides merchandising-specific business intelligence within Oracle Retail Insights. It delivers insight into critical performance indicators including item sales, store performance, markdowns, sales trends, and profit contribution across the product and organisation hierarchies. The Merchandising Sales & Profit subject area enables buyers, planners, and executives to monitor and act on merchandising performance at every level — from company down to individual item — using three analysis modes: As-Is, As-Was, and Point in Time.

## 2.3 Key Business Questions
Which items are my top 10 sellers for a selected period and department range? How does each division's sales and profit contribution compare to last year? What are my markdown-to-sales ratios WTD, MTD, and YTD vs. last year? How are seasonal merchandise assortments performing in terms of sales and profitability? Are my daily store and regional sales projections being met? Which locations are showing negative variance against the sales forecast this week?

## 3. Subject Areas & Analysis Methods
The Merchandising Sales & Profit reporting is delivered through the Retail Merchandise Insights subject areas in Oracle BI. There are three subject areas, each supporting a different analysis method for the slowly changing Product and Organisation dimensions. Note: As-Is and As-Was results cannot be mixed on the same report. Use separate dashboard pages for each analysis mode.

## 4. Dashboards & Predefined Reports
The following predefined reports are packaged with Oracle Retail Insights under the Retail Merchandise Insights dashboard. They are organised into two sections: Merchandising Scorecard and Merchandising Analysis.

## 4.2.3 Current Sales & Profit Contribution (3 Sub-Reports)
This report provides a view of sales and profit contribution across the organisation by merchandising division. It can be run monthly to compare the merchandising mix this year to last year. Three sub-reports are included: Navigation: For underperforming divisions, users can navigate to the Current Location Scorecard report via Guided Navigation to analyse division performance by location.

## Assumptions
Nightly batch ETL via Oracle Data Integrator (ODI) completes successfully before reports are accessed. RMS is the primary source for product, organisation, promotion, and calendar dimension data. MFP provides sales forecast data at item–location–week granularity. Predefined reports are used without structural modification unless explicitly scoped and tested.

## Constraints
Planning/stock-ledger reports cannot be created below subclass and week level. As-Is and As-Was analysis modes cannot be combined on a single report. Point in Time reports require a time dimension prompt and cannot use aggregate fact tables. Season-based reporting is not supported for Market Item and Consumer reports. Items in multiple seasons require a filter on season to avoid double-counting. — End of Document —

## Table 1
Document Version | 1.0
Status | Draft
Date | May 2026
Module | Merchandising Analysis – Sales & Profit
Source | Oracle Retail Insights User Guide (2016)

## Table 2
# | Objective
1 | Provide a high-level, organisation-wide view of merchandising strategy effectiveness.
2 | Enable buyers to identify top-selling items and evaluate pricing and promotion strategies.
3 | Allow merchandising executives to compare sales and profit contribution across divisions this year vs. last year.
4 | Support markdown strategy evaluation by comparing markdown-to-sales ratios across retail price types (regular, promotion, clearance).
5 | Enable planners and buyers to analyse seasonal merchandise assortment performance.
6 | Allow regional and store managers to monitor daily sales and profit against projections.
7 | Support mid-week assessment of actual sales quantities vs. forecast by location.

## Table 3
Subject Area | Description
Retail Merchandise Insights As-Is | Historical data is associated with the current (post-reclassification) hierarchy. Shows performance as if it always occurred under today's structure.
Retail Merchandise Insights As-Was | Historical data stays linked to the hierarchy that was in place at the time of the transaction. Enables before/after reclassification comparison.
Retail Merchandise Insights Point in Time | Hierarchy is applied as it existed on a user-supplied date. Requires a time dimension prompt on every report.

## Table 4
Section | Dashboard | Report Name | Analysis Method | Primary Users
Merchandising Scorecard | Markdowns | Current Markdown Scorecard – Markdown to Sales Ratio | As-Was | Merch Exec, Finance Exec, Buyers
Merchandising Scorecard | Merchandise Sales & Profit | Current Top 10 Sale Items | As-Was / As-Is | Buyers, Merch Exec
Merchandising Scorecard | Merchandise Sales & Profit | Current Sales & Profit Contribution – Sales LY | As-Was | Merch Exec, Finance Exec
Merchandising Scorecard | Merchandise Sales & Profit | Current Sales & Profit Contribution – Profit LY | As-Was | Merch Exec, Finance Exec
Merchandising Scorecard | Merchandise Sales & Profit | Current Sales & Profit Contribution – Total | As-Was | Merch Exec, Finance Exec
Merchandising Scorecard | Merchandise Performance | Season Performance | As-Was | Planners, Buyers
Merchandising Analysis | Merchandising Location Analysis | Daily Sales & Profit | As-Was | Regional/Store Managers
Merchandising Analysis | Merchandising Location Analysis | Current Sales Projection | As-Was | Merch/Planning Exec, Inventory Mgr

## Table 5
Dashboard | Markdowns
Analysis Method | As-Was
Business Purpose | Displays WTD, MTD, and YTD retail markdown-to-sales ratios for the current year vs. last year, broken down by regular, promotion, and clearance retail types.
Business Decision | Determine effectiveness of markdown strategies; identify items with high markdown variance vs. LY for supplier negotiation.
Key Metrics | Mkdn to Sales Amt WTD/MTD/YTD, Mkdn to Sales Amt LY WTD/MTD/YTD, Mkdn Amt (Clr/Pro/Pmt), Mkup Amt
Filters / Prompts | Time Period, Location (Region/Store), Department

## Table 6
Dashboard | Merchandise Sales & Profit
Analysis Method | As-Was (also As-Is version available)
Business Purpose | Shows the top ten selling items ranked by sales amount for a user-specified time period and department range.
Business Decision | Evaluate pricing and promotion strategies for key items; review merchandising strategies periodically.
Key Metrics | Net Sales Amt, Gross Sales Amt, Net Sales Qty, Net Profit, Sales Amt Item Contribution to Department
Filters / Prompts | Time Period, Department range, Location

## Table 7
Sub-Report | Content
Sales LY | Gross sales amounts by division; sales contribution % this year and last year.
Profit LY | Profit amounts by division; profit contribution % this year and last year.
Total | Gross sales, sales contribution %, gross profit, and profit contribution % for all divisions combined.

## Table 8
Dashboard | Merchandise Performance
Analysis Method | As-Was
Business Purpose | Displays performance across departments for a specified product season. Product seasons do not need to align with the business calendar.
Business Decision | Compare sales and profitability of seasonal assortments; support season-based merchandise assortment decisions.
Key Metrics | Net Sales Amt, Net Profit, Gross Sales Amt, Season Start/End Date, Dept performance by season
Filters / Prompts | Product Season, Department, Location
Constraint | Season-based reporting is NOT supported for Market Item and Consumer Reports. Items common to multiple seasons must be filtered to avoid double-counting.

## Table 9
Dashboard | Merchandising Location Analysis
Analysis Method | As-Was
Business Purpose | Provides an organisational comparison of sales and profit trends compared to the same time period last year. Run daily by regional and store managers.
Business Decision | Ensure daily projections for regions and locations are being met on high-traffic days; trigger corrective actions when targets are missed.
Key Metrics | Net Sales Amt, Gross Profit, Net Profit, Net Sales Amt LY, Net Profit LY, Net Sales Amt Var LY
Filters / Prompts | Date, Region, Store / Location, Department

## Table 10
Dashboard | Merchandising Location Analysis
Analysis Method | As-Was
Business Purpose | Displays actual sales quantities compared to forecast for the current week, broken down by location.
Business Decision | Mid-week assessment of forecast variance; inventory control managers can investigate whether low stock is causing under-performance vs. forecast.
Key Metrics | Gross Sales Qty, Fcst Sales Qty, Fcst Sales Qty Var, Gross Sales Qty WTD Var LY
Filters / Prompts | Week, Location, Department
Conditional Formatting | Threshold-based colour coding: variance above high threshold → green; below low threshold → red. Thresholds are user-configurable.

## Table 11
Metric | Definition
Net Sales Amt | Sales amount excluding returns; actual money received from sales.
Gross Sales Amt | Total amount from all units sold (before returns).
Net Sales Qty / Gross Sales Qty | Net/gross number of units sold.
Return Amt / Return Qty | Value and quantity of units returned.
Net Profit | Bottom-line profit after accounting for returns.
Gross Profit | Difference between sales revenue and cost of units sold.
Net Sales Amt LY / Var LY | Last year's net sales; variance (A-B)/B vs. last year.
Net Sales Amt WTD/MTD/YTD | Week-to-date, month-to-date, year-to-date net sales.
Sales Amt Contribution to Division | Sales revenue for a division as % of company total.
Profit Item Contribution to Dept | Profit from an item as % of total department profit.
Trx Count | Number of transactions.

## Table 12
Metric | Definition
Supplier Base Cost | Initial cost before any charges, discounts or deals.
Supplier Net Cost | Base cost after trade, cash, and off-invoice discounts.
Supplier Net Net Cost | Net cost less any bill-back amounts.
Supplier Dead Net Cost | Net net cost less any rebate amounts.
Supplier Base Profit | Sales revenue minus supplier base cost.
Supplier Net Profit | Profit calculated from supplier net cost.
Supplier Net Net Profit | Profit calculated from supplier net net cost.
Supplier Dead Net Profit | Profit calculated from supplier dead net cost.

## Table 13
Metric | Definition
Mkdn Amt | Total markdown amount (clearance + promotion + permanent).
Clr / Pro / Pmt Mkdn Amt | Clearance, promotion, permanent markdown amounts.
Mkup Amt | Total markup amount.
Mkdn to Sales Amt | Ratio of markdown amount to gross sales amount.
Mkdn Amt WTD/MTD/YTD | Week-, month-, year-to-date markdown amounts.
Mkdn to Sales Amt LY WTD/MTD/YTD | Last-year markdown-to-sales ratios by period.
Mkdn Amt Var LY | Markdown amount variance compared to last year.
Comp Mkdn Amt | Markdown amount in comparable stores only.
Gross Markdown % | Actual percentage of markdowns taken against an item or category.

## Table 14
Metric | Definition
Fcst Sales Qty | Forecast quantity of sales units for the given period.
Fcst Sales Qty LW/MTD/YTD | Last-week, month-to-date, year-to-date forecast quantities.
Fcst Sales Qty Var | Gross sales quantity variance vs. forecast.
Fcst Sales Qty NW | Next week's forecast quantity.
Fcst Sales Qty MTD/YTD Var | MTD/YTD variance of actuals vs. forecast.

## Table 15
Dimension | Hierarchy | Key Attributes
Product | Company → Division → Group → Dept → Class → Subclass → Item | Division, Group, Dept, Class, Subclass, Item; Style/Colour differentiators; Profit Calc Type; Purchase Type
Organisation | Company → Chain → Area → Region → District → Store/Location | Channel, Store Format, Selling Area, Comp Store Flag, VAT Region, Currency Code, Store Class
Business Calendar | Year → Half → Quarter → Period → Week → Day | Fiscal Year, Fiscal Quarter, Fiscal Period, Fiscal Week, Fiscal Date; supports 4-5-4, 13-Period, and Gregorian
Product Season | Season → Phase → Item | Season ID, Season Desc, Season Start/End Date, Phase
Comparable Store | N/A – flag on Organisation | Comp Store Flag: derived from source system or calculated by RI. Filters out new/closed stores from baseline comparisons.

## Table 16
Req ID | Requirement | Priority | Source
FR-001 | The system shall provide the Retail Merchandise Insights dashboard with Merchandising Scorecard and Merchandising Analysis sections. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-002 | The Merchandise Sales & Profit dashboard shall include Current Top 10 Sale Items (As-Was and As-Is versions) and the Current Sales & Profit Contribution report with all three sub-reports. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-003 | The Markdowns dashboard shall include the Current Markdown Scorecard – Markdown to Sales Ratio report displaying WTD, MTD, and YTD markdown-to-sales ratios for current year and last year. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-004 | The Merchandise Performance dashboard shall include the Season Performance report. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-005 | The Merchandising Location Analysis dashboard shall include Daily Sales & Profit and Current Sales Projection reports. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-006 | All reports shall support dashboard-level prompts for time period, organisation hierarchy (region/store), and product hierarchy (division/department). | Must Have | User Guide
FR-007 | The Current Sales Projection report shall support user-configurable conditional formatting thresholds for Gross Sales Qty WTD Var LY (green = above high threshold, red = below low threshold). | Must Have | User Guide
FR-008 | The Current Sales & Profit Contribution report shall support guided navigation to the Current Location Scorecard report for underperforming divisions. | Should Have | User Guide
FR-009 | All amount metrics shall support five currencies: Local, Document, Global 1, Global 2, and Global 3. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-010 | Reports shall support drilling on Product hierarchy (Division → Group → Dept → Class → Subclass → Item) and Organisation hierarchy (Company → Region → Store). | Must Have | User Guide
FR-011 | Sales facts shall be stored and reported by retail price type: Regular, Promotion, and Clearance. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-012 | Sales facts shall be held at the item–location–day level and the subclass–location–week level to support both detailed and aggregate reporting. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-013 | The Season Performance report shall allow product seasons that do not align with the business calendar. A prompt or filter on season shall be required to prevent double-counting of items belonging to multiple seasons. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-014 | Sales forecast data shall be stored at the item–location–week level. Forecast sales quantities shall exclude VAT. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-015 | Comparable store metrics shall exclude new or closed stores. The Comp Store Flag shall be derivable either from the source system or computed internally by RI using the store open date. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-016 | Comp and BOH (beginning on-hand) metrics shall only be supported at week level and require a prompt or filter on week or higher. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-017 | Point in Time reports shall require a prompt on an attribute of the time dimension. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-018 | As-Is and As-Was results shall not be mixed on the same report; they shall appear on separate dashboard pages. | Must Have | User Guide
FR-019 | Planning and stock ledger reports shall not be created below subclass and week granularity. | Must Have | User Guide

## Table 17
Category | Requirement
Data Currency | Reports must reflect data from a completed nightly batch ETL run. Reports shall not be rendered if the batch for the subject area has not completed successfully.
Role-Based Access | Access shall be governed by roles: Buyers, Buyer Analysts, Inventory Analysts, Inventory Managers, Merchandising Executives, Merchandise Financial Planners, Planning Executives, Promotional Planners, Pricing Analysts.
Data-Level Security | Retail Insights does not provide data-level security. Row-level access control must be managed by upstream data provisioning if required.
Multi-Language | The module shall support all RI-supported languages including English, French, German, Spanish, Japanese, Chinese (Simplified & Traditional), and others.
Report Integrity | Moving, removing, or re-ordering columns or prompts on predefined reports is not recommended; reports have only been tested in their current configuration.
Source Systems | Sales data: Oracle Retail Sales Audit (ReSA). Product/Org/Promotion dimensions: Oracle Retail Merchandising System (RMS). Forecast data: Oracle Retail Merchandise Financial Planning (MFP). Invoice cost: Oracle Retail Invoice Matching (ReIM). Pricing/promotion: Oracle Retail Price Management (RPM).
